repositories.name: requests
repositories.reason: Reads cleanly. A single-language library, and the cheapest signal that ordinary Python still parses.

repositories.name: express
repositories.reason: Reads cleanly. Plain JavaScript with no build step, so nothing here is transpiler-specific.

repositories.name: ripgrep
repositories.reason: Reads cleanly. Idiomatic Rust including macros, which is where the call rules go blind.

repositories.name: zod
repositories.reason: Four files use TypeScript 4.7 variance annotations on type parameters, which tree-sitter-typescript does not implement: tree-sitter/tree-sitter-typescript#364. Everything else in those files is still read.

repositories.name: deno
repositories.reason: Rust and TypeScript in one tree, which is why it is here. Six files are deliberately not valid UTF-8, being encoding test fixtures. The rest are syntax the grammars do not implement.

repositories.name: vscode
repositories.reason: The largest TypeScript tree in the corpus. One file is above the four-mebibyte read ceiling, which is the ceiling working rather than a defect.

repositories.name: sentry
repositories.reason: A monolith with Python and TSX side by side. 408 of these are .tsx, nearly all one construct: a generic type argument on a call followed by a template literal, as in styled('a')<{disabled?: boolean}>`...`, which the tsx grammar does not parse. Three are Python type-parameter defaults from PEP 696. This budget is the largest single argument for teaching the grammars both forms.

repositories.name: home-assistant
repositories.reason: The largest Python tree in the corpus, at eighteen thousand files. Every entry is PEP 696 type-parameter defaults, which tree-sitter-python does not implement.
